}}'''Berelain sur Paendrag Paeron''' (BEH-reh-lain suhr PAY-ehn-DRAG; /ˈbɛ.ɹɛ.ɫeɪn sʊɹ ˈpeɪ.ɛnˌdɹæg/), Blessed of the Light, [[Defender of the Waves]], [[High Seat]] of [[House Paeron]], is the [[First of Mayene|First]] of [[Mayene]].

==Appearance==
She is a beautiful, tall, pale woman with long black hair to her shoulders, and has large, dark eyes. She wears the [[Diadem of the First]], a golden hawk in flight. She is noted by virtually everyone who encounters her as being exceptionally voluptuous both in appearance and action. She is fully aware of her own beauty and its effects on others, and makes full use of her appearance to further her political, diplomatic, and personal goals.

==History==
She was born in {{ne|974}}, and her mother died when she was nine. She loved her father desperately - partly because her mother had been cold, partly because he returned her affection. She became High Seat of House Paeron and First of Mayene in {{ne|984}} at age ten, and had a regent/guardian until turning sixteen in {{ne|990}}. Her younger brothers and sister were all Seconds of Mayene.

At age sixteen, she banished her guardian; he was dour, strict, and incompatible with her own personality. However, she knew him to be honest, dutiful, and loyal. Therefore, she brought him back to watch over the Seconds when she left Mayene.

She often behaves in a spoiled, petulant manner. Yet she is also pragmatic, a necessary trait to allow small and relatively weak Mayene to survive next to large and powerful neighbors like [[Tear]]. She believed in learning as much as possible about the people she had to deal with.

Berelain claims to be a descendant and heir of [[Artur Hawkwing]] through his grandson [[Tyrn sur Paendrag Mashera]]. In Mayene it is claimed that Tyrn evaded the assassination attempt that killed his mother and was raised in secrecy in Mayene for his own safety. The Firsts of Mayene claim an unbroken line of succession from Tyrn and his daughter [[Miselle]], and through him to Hawkwing. This claim is not taken seriously outside of Mayene.

==Activities==
She was a 'guest' within the [[Stone of Tear]] since before the winter of {{Ne|998}}/{{Ne|999}}. [[Lan]] mentions she announced she would submit to the will of the High Lords the day after she had said "she would see Mayene and all its ships burn before one Tairen country lord set foot in the country". This is taken by Lan as evidence of [[Rand]]'s ''[[ta'veren]]'' effects in Tear.{{ref/book|3|53}}

Berelain brings a note to [[Moiraine Damodred|Moiraine]] the day after [[Rand al'Thor]] takes ''[[Callandor]]''. The note, signed by [[Lanfear]], claims possession of "[[Lews Therin Telamon|Lews Therin]]" but leaves him in the temporary care of Moiraine. Berelain tells [[Rhuarc]] that she will dine with him, as he is the apparent leader of the [[Aiel]] occupying the Stone.{{ref/book|3|56}} Later, Berelain was apparently rebuffed and given a 'talk' by [[Rhuarc]].{{ref/book|3|14}}}}

===Chasing Perrin===
[[File:Berelain.jpg|thumb|left|308x308px|Berelain sur Paendrag Paeron Portrait by Seamas Gallagher]]
Following the fall of the [[Stone of Tear]], Berelain tries to seduce Rand in his chambers in an effort to obtain political influence, but is rebuffed. During her attempted seduction, a [[bubble of evil]] causes Rand's reflections to come out of a mirror and try to kill him. Berelain was terrified by the experience, and she never tried to seduce Rand again.{{ref/book|4|2}} When [[Matrim Cauthon]] tries to charm her she ignores him, implying she views him as being too much like herself.{{ref/book|4|13}} Instead, she turns her attentions on [[Perrin Aybara]].{{ref/book|4|14}} Perrin rejects her advances, but she is undeterred. Her actions spark a fierce rivalry with [[Faile Bashere]], with Berelain claiming it will "amuse" her to take Perrin away from Faile.{{ref/book|4|14}}

Later, Rand places Berelain in a position of stewardship over the city of [[Cairhien]] after it is ravaged by the [[Shaido]] [[Aiel]].{{ref/book|6|14}} During this time she neglects her duties in Cairhien enough that she receives a stern reminder from [[Rhuarc]],{{ref/book|6|32}} who treats her as a daughter. Later, after Perrin arrives in Cairhien, Berelain renews her pursuit of him. Her flirtation causes tension between Perrin and his wife Faile. When Rand is captured by the [[White Tower]] [[Aes Sedai]], she uncovers evidence linking [[Colavaere Saighan]] to both [[Lord Maringil]]'s and [[Meilan Mendiana]]'s murders as part of Colavaere's plot for the [[Sun Throne]].{{ref/book|6|53}} Though she cannot use this evidence without Rand, she informs Perrin and sends soldiers to Rand's aid.{{ref/book|6|54}}

While Rand is missing, Colavaere is crowned Queen. As queen, Colavaere takes Berelain's Aes Sedai adviser [[Annoura Larisen]] for her own and relegates Berelain from steward of Cairhien to one of her ladies in waiting. Colavaere also makes Faile a lady in waiting and is amused by the tension between the two romantic rivals.{{ref/book|7|6}} When Rand returns to Cairhien, Berelain publicly denounces Colavaere's crimes, which Colavaere corroborates under Rand's ''[[ta'veren]]'' influence. Despite her many services to him, Rand does not reinstate Berelain as steward after Colavaere's fall, but instead tries to send her back to Mayene. She prevails upon him to send her with Perrin to [[Ghealdan]] to track down [[Masema Dagar]] instead.{{ref/book|7|27}}

===Ghealdan===
[[File:Berelain sur Paendrag Paeron.JPG|right|thumb|299x299px|Berelain sur Paendrag Paeron by Todd Cameron Hamilton]]
Perrin sends her to meet with Queen [[Alliandre Maritha Kigarin]]. She brings Alliandre back to camp where Alliandre swears fealty to Perrin. Later, Berelain helps Faile pressure Alliandre into keeping her oath of fealty to Perrin by staying with the army. While out hunting with Faile and Alliandre, the group is attacked by the Shaido Aiel. All of the group are captured except Berelain, who manages to escape and send word to Perrin.{{ref/book|8|30}}

While Faile is in captivity, Berelain at first tries to offer a truce to Perrin in regards to her advances, but his reaction affronts her.{{ref/book|9|5}} She then allows rumors to be spread around the camp that he succumbed to her advances, causing Perrin's own men and even devoted [[Aram]] to lose respect for him.{{ref/book|9|5}} Despite this, she still serves as Perrin's political and strategic ally. She is instrumental in discovering [[Masema]]'s collusion with the [[Seanchan]]{{ref/book|10|6}}, and offers to use her gold and jewels to ransom the Shaido's prisoners, including Faile.{{ref/book|10|8}} She accompanies Perrin to [[So Habor]], where they collect grain for their troops. When they return to their camp she witnesses an interrogation in which Perrin cleaves off a Shaido prisoner's hand in his desperation to get information on Faile.

===Plan to rescue Faile===
Berelain is present when [[Galina Casban]] is brought before Perrin and questioned. Galina asks to be slapped so she can claim she was beaten by brigands, and Berelain complies.
She later goes with Perrin when he makes his deal with the [[Seanchan]].

She is present at the meeting with Perrin and [[Tylee Khirgan]], who informs Perrin of a rebellious group of [[Whitecloaks]] moving north not too far from camp, when the [[Pattern]] ripples.

While traveling back through Ghealdan after the [[Battle of Malden]] she is with Perrin when they find land that appears to have been affected by the [[Blight]]. Later, she attends a meeting with Perrin to decide where the army should now go. A decision is made to send a scouting force to Cairhien to start looking for Rand.

Faile confronts Berelain about the rumors of her bedding Perrin while Faile was captive. At first Faile issues a challenge but on further discussion they decide to be seen around camp as friends to help dissuade the rumors; they decide that Berelain cannot simply publicly denounce the rumors as it would not be convincing enough.

=== Meeting the man in White ===
[[file:WoT Japanese CoT2.gif|thumb|left|Berelain wearing the Diadem of the First (from a [[Wheel of Time translations|Japanese]] translation book cover)]]
Berelain is present during the second parley between Perrin and [[Galadedrid Damodred]], and the pair are immediately attracted to each other. She is walking through the camp when a [[bubble of evil]] causes weapons to attack their owners. Faile rescues her when she throws dirt onto the dagger that is attacking her, causing it to become inanimate again. Faile saving Berelain's life seems to have finally quelled all rumors of Perrin's alleged infidelity with her.

Berelain keeps asking Perrin if she can negotiate with Galad and blushes when she sees him at Perrin's trial.

Berelain is present when Perrin creates ''[[Mah'alleinir]]'' and then declares to his followers his acceptance at becoming their Lord and leader. Perrin then gives the command for his army to [[Traveling|Travel]] back to where the Whitecloaks have set up their camp. Berelain is concerned that Perrin is planning to ambush the Whitecloaks and Faile reassures her that such an act is not in Perrin's character. Berelain admits that she has finally given up on Perrin and sets her sights on Galad, hence her concern for the Whitecloaks.

Perrin sends her, Alliandre, and Faile to the back of his army when his force starts attacking the Trollocs as they begin springing their ambush on the Whitecloaks. This helps alleviate her fears that Perrin will attack the Whitecloaks. After the battle, the three ladies help cut bandages for the injured. Berelain admits to Faile the reason she tried to seduce Perrin was to tie herself to the Dragon Reborn through one of his good friends. She attends Morgase and [[Martyn Tallanvor]]'s wedding with Galad.

Berelain Travels with Perrin and the rest of his army to the [[Field of Merrilor]] to prepare for the [[Last Battle]]. While there, she signs the [[Dragon's Peace]] as ruler of Mayene.

As the Last Battle commences, she returns to Mayene to oversee a Healing center stationed there. She is there when an injured Galad is brought by [[Annoura Larisen|Annoura]]. She is also responsible for sending Galad's ''ter'angreal'' to [[Lan Mandragoran|Lan]], helping Lan defeat [[Demandred]].

==Viewing==
A [[Min's viewings|viewing]] by [[Min Farshaw]] indicates that she will fall in love with a man in white.{{ref/book|6|50}} This, combined with a viewing of two most beautiful people falling in love, seems to indicate that she will marry [[Galad Damodred]].

==Parallels==
Berelain could be a reference to the name Elaine, which was the name of several different women in Arthurian legend — particularly Elaine of Astolat, who died of unrequited love for Lancelot. Her surname, Paendrag, derives from the name of Uther Pendragon, King Arthur's father.

Berelain could also be based upon Eva Perón, the famous Argentinian woman who became a hero to her people and came from humble background (akin to how Berelain is leader of the smallest of nations).

Berelain also has some parallels with Cleopatra, the historical queen of Egypt who was renowned for her beauty, sexuality, and political acumen. Cleopatra snuck into Julius Caesar's presence to seduce him and gain his support, much like Berelain sneaks into Rand's chambers in TSR. After Caesar's assassination, Cleopatra played different sides in the conflicts between Caesar's successors - not unlike Berelain joining Colavaere's court after Rand's abduction from Cairhien. Eventually Cleopatra partnered with Mark Antony, whom Shakespeare characterizes as a moralizer in his speech in ''Julius Caesar'' where Mark Antony stirs up sympathy for Caesar just after his murder. Cleopatra had a very passionate love affair with Mark Antony. Berelain also falls in love with notable moralizer and political/martial leader, Galadedred Damodred.
